title: Learning-by-exporting in South Africa: the influence of global value chain (GVC) participation and technological capability
publisher: African Journal of Science, Technology, Innovation and Development 16(4), 459–476
summary: The paper examines how trade related to global value chains affects the performance of manufacturing firms in South Africa. GVC-related trade carries a higher productivity premium than traditional trade, but only firms that also invest in R&D appear to learn from exporting.
keyFindings: GVC-related trade is associated with a higher productivity premium than traditional trade.
Only firms trading in GVC-related products that also engage in R&D after entry appear to learn from exporting.
GVC-integrated firms need to invest in building technological capacity.
methods: Firm-level panel data from SARS and National Treasury, 2009–2017, comparing productivity premia across product classifications before and after export entry.
